To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
YouTube’s traffic is not affected by the available bandwidth, but the video’s quality is.
the YouTube video player is able to adapt the consumed bitrate to the available download bandwidth, and that the consumed bandwidth is not constant during the whole video playback.
the allowed download bandwidth for a YouTube video is 3.5 times higher than the consumed bitrate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of YouTube’s video traffic in order to provide an understanding of the YouTube’s video streaming service, and also the YouTube’s traffic adaptation behavior to the network environment.
a YouTube’s traffic characterization and performance analysis, in order to provide valuable information for QoS/QoE management.
the analysis of YouTube’s traffic pattern and its relation to QoS/QoE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, YouTube’s traffic is very dynamic and it is not possible to provide a fixed QoS to the end user.
YouTube’s traffic is not able to fully utilize the available download bandwidth, even when the available bandwidth is high enough.
, in order to obtain a target end-user QoE for YouTube’s traffic, it is required to know the YouTube’s traffic pattern, and to assure an adequate download bandwidth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
YouTube’s traffic adaptation has been analyzed and the results are valuable for the QoS and QoE management of the Internet service providers.
we have been able to analyze YouTube’s DASH traffic in a more detailed way than it has been done in the past.
the obtained results can be applied for QoE management, and that they are also a good basis for future work.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the download bandwidth of YouTube videos is a good metric to be used in QoS management.
, in order to provide QoS and QoE management for YouTube’s video streaming, ISPs should take into consideration the particularities of YouTube’s DASH traffic.
the download bandwidth of YouTube’s video player is the main factor to determine the consumed bitrate and, therefore, the video quality.
